samples.input:
Use a surfaceId of 'main'. Generate a 'createSurface' message to describe the following UI:

A vertical list with:
- Dog breed information
- Dog generator

The dog breed information is a card, which contains a title “Famous Dog breeds”, a header image, and a horizontal list of images of different dog breeds (using a 'List' component). The list information should be in the data model at /breeds.

The dog generator is another card which is a form that generates a fictional dog breed with a description
- Title
- Description text explaining what it is
- Dog breed name (text input)
- Number of legs (number input)
- Button called “Generate” which takes the data above and generates a new dog description
- Skills (ChoicePicker component, variant 'multipleSelection')
- A divider
- A section which shows the generated content
samples.target: A valid A2UI payload with surfaceId 'main' . The UI must include a vertical list with a 'Famous Dog breeds' card (header image, horizontal list of breeds) and a 'Dog generator' card (form with Title, Description, name input, legs input, 'Generate' button, skills ChoicePicker, and result section).

## Instructions:
# A2UI Atom Output Contract

You must output the user interface using the compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with the sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize data model state using (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) or (data $/map_path (:key1 "val1" :key2 "val2")).

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value). Interactive controls with action attributes MUST provide an action expression, e.g., (ActionComponent :child (ChildComponent "Text") :action (Event "click_action")).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :action (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [(:id 1 :name "Item 1")] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence & Conciseness:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).
   - Output minimal properties required to satisfy the user request.



Additional Rules:
1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.

<a2ui>
(Column :id "root"
  (data
    $/breeds [
      (:name "Golden Retriever" :imgUrl "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1552053831-71594a27632d?auto=format&fit=crop&q=80&w=300")
      (:name "Siberian Husky" :imgUrl "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1531804055935-76f44d7c3621?auto=format&fit=crop&q=80&w=300")
      (:name "French Bulldog" :imgUrl "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1583511655857-d19b40a7a54e?auto=format&fit=crop&q=80&w=300")
    ]
    $/generator/skillsOptions [
      (:value "laserEyes" :label "Laser Eyes")
      (:value "flight" :label "Flight")
      (:value "telepathy" :label "Telepathy")
      (:value "superBark" :label "Super Bark")
    ]
    $/generator/breedName ""
    $/generator/numLegs "4"
    $/generator/selectedSkills []
    $/generator/generatedResult "Your generated breed details will appear here once you click Generate."
  )

  ;; Card 1: Famous Dog Breeds Info
  (Card :child
    (Column
      (Text :text "Famous Dog breeds" :variant "body")
      (Image :url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543466835-00a7907e9de1?auto=format&fit=crop&q=80&w=800" :description "Famous dog breeds banner" :variant "header")
      (List :direction "horizontal" :children
        (template :item breed
          (Column
            (Image :url $/breed/imgUrl :description $/breed/name :variant "smallFeature")
            (Text :text $/breed/name :variant "caption")
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )

  ;; Card 2: Dog Generator Form
  (Card :child
    (Column
      (Text :text "Dog Breed Generator" :variant "body")
      (Text :text "Design and create your custom fictional dog breed by configuring the genetic traits below." :variant "caption")

      (TextField
        :label "Dog Breed Name"
        :value $/generator/breedName
        :placeholder "Enter custom breed name"
        :variant "shortText"
      )

      (TextField
        :label "Number of Legs"
        :value $/generator/numLegs
        :placeholder "e.g. 4"
        :variant "number"
      )

      (ChoicePicker
        :label "Skills"
        :variant "multipleSelection"
        :options $/generator/skillsOptions
        :value $/generator/selectedSkills
        :displayStyle "chips"
      )

      (Divider :axis "horizontal")

      (Button
        :child (Text :text "Generate")
        :variant "primary"
        :action (Event "generate_breed"
                  :name $/generator/breedName
                  :legs $/generator/numLegs
                  :skills $/generator/selectedSkills
                )
      )

      ;; Generated Content Section
      (Column
        (Text :text "Generated Fictional Breed" :variant "body")
        (Text :text $/generator/generatedResult :variant "caption")
      )
    )

You are an AI assistant. Based on the following request, generate a user interface.

## Instructions:
# A2UI Atom Output Contract

You must output the user interface using the compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with the sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize data model state using (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) or (data $/map_path (:key1 "val1" :key2 "val2")).

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value). Interactive controls with action attributes MUST provide an action expression, e.g., (ActionComponent :child (ChildComponent "Text") :action (Event "click_action")).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :action (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [(:id 1 :name "Item 1")] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence & Conciseness:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).
   - Output minimal properties required to satisfy the user request.



Additional Rules:
1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.


## Component Catalog Signatures:
- (AudioPlayer :url :description? :weight?)
  - :url: The URL of the audio to be played.
  - :description: A description of the audio, such as a title or summary.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (Button :child :variant? :action :weight? :checks?)
  - :child: The ID of the child component. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button. Only use an 'Icon' if the requirements explicitly ask for an icon-only button. Do NOT define the child component inline.
  - :variant: A hint for the button style. If omitted, a default button style is used. 'primary' indicates this is the main call-to-action button. 'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link. Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (Card :child :weight?)
  - :child: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card. To display multiple elements, you MUST wrap them in a layout component (like Column or Row) and pass that container's ID here. Do NOT pass multiple IDs or a non-existent ID. Do NOT define the child component inline.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (CheckBox :label :value :weight? :checks?)
  - :label: The text to display next to the checkbox.
  - :value: The current state of the checkbox (true for checked, false for unchecked).
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (ChoicePicker :label? :variant? :options :value :displayStyle? :filterable? :weight? :checks?)
  - A component that allows selecting one or more options from a list.
  - :label: The label for the group of options.
  - :variant: A hint for how the choice picker should be displayed and behave. Must be one of: 'multipleSelection', 'mutuallyExclusive'
  - :options: The list of available options to choose from.

**Product Gallery Initialization - A Detailed Thought Process**

Alright, let's break this down. My objective is crystal clear: initialize a product gallery UI on the 'main' surface. This requires a root component with the ID 'root' and, crucially, a data model at the path `/products` populated with at least two products, each having the essential 'id', 'name', and 'imageUrl' keys.

The data model needs to be set up at `/products` at the *beginning* of the root or somewhere nested. Let's make it easy on ourselves and use a map-like structure for `/products`, as requested in the instructions.

After thinking about it, here is how to structure it, as per the rules:

```
(data $/products (:product1 (:id "product1" :name "Awesome Gadget" :imageUrl "https://picsum.photos/id/10/300/200") :product2 (:id "product2" :name "Sleek Smartwatch" :imageUrl "https://picsum.photos/id/11/300/200")))
```

That's the basic data set up. Now, to display it. I can use the example to help guide me.  Since I want to show a map, I can reference specific paths like `$/products/product1/name`. I will statically render two products with cards.

Okay, let's design the UI. I will begin with the Root component. Then add the data set up:

```lisp
(Column :id "root"
  (data $/products (:product1 (:id "product1" :name "Awesome Gadget" :imageUrl "https://picsum.photos/id/10/300/300") :product2 (:id "product2" :name "Sleek Smartwatch" :imageUrl "https://picsum.photos/id/48/300/300")))
  ...)
```

  *  A Card with the image, text, and button for each product

```lisp

(Column :id "root"
  (data $/products (:product1 (:id "product1" :name "Awesome Gadget" :imageUrl "https://picsum.photos/id/10/300/300") :product2 (:id "product2" :name "Sleek Smartwatch" :imageUrl "https://picsum.photos/id/48/300/300")))

      (Button :child (Text :text "View Product") :action (Event "view_product" :id "product2") :variant "primary")))))
</a2ui>
```

*   Does the child nest?
*   Do the properties match?
*  Do I need to nest the data?

Yes! No need to use any ID parameters. Every component is nested.

-   `Text`: Text content comes from data paths, and the display variant is correct.
-   `Image`:  Image URLs are from data paths, and fit, and the style variants are used.
-   `Button`: Text components as child, correct actions, and variant.
-   `Card`: Uses `Column` as a child and is nested.

Okay, here's my breakdown of how I'm approaching this. The goal is to create a User Settings UI with specific components on the 'main' surface. I must use a strict tree nesting structure, no flat references or explicit IDs. I have to build it with Tabs, a Modal, and some data initialization, as described.

First, I identified the required components: Tabs with "Profile" and "# Notifications" tabs, each containing a specific layout. There is also a "Delete Account" button that triggers a confirmation Modal. The Modal needs confirmation and cancel buttons.

Next, I examined the component catalog carefully. I noticed that the `Tabs`, `Modal`, `Button`, `Column`, `Row`, and other signatures all describe children as properties like `:child` or `:children`. However, the instructions state "Children cannot be defined inline, they must be referred to by ID," which seems contradictory to the rule "nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions". I should use positional children and the keyword properties (e.g. `:child`, `:tabs`), to comply with both the catalog *and* the strict tree nesting.

Data state needs initialization, so I'll use `(data ...)` inside the outermost `Column` to initialize the data model.

You are an AI assistant. Based on the following request, generate a user interface.

## Instructions:
# A2UI Atom Output Contract

You must output the user interface using the compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with the sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize data model state using (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) or (data $/map_path (:key1 "val1" :key2 "val2")).

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value). Interactive controls with action attributes MUST provide an action expression, e.g., (ActionComponent :child (ChildComponent "Text") :action (Event "click_action")).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :action (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [(:id 1 :name "Item 1")] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence & Conciseness:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).
   - Output minimal properties required to satisfy the user request.



Additional Rules:
1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.

'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link. Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.

  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.

**My Thought Process: Building a User Profile UI with A2UI**

Okay, so the goal is to create a user interface to display and allow editing of a logged-in user's profile. I need to initialize the 'main' surface with a data model containing the user's name and email, and then construct a UI that reflects this.  The core requirement is to start with a data initialization statement with the path `/user/name` as "John Doe" and `/user/email` as "john.doe@example.com".

First, I need to design the interface components. I will create a root component, let's go with a `Column`, and I'll make sure it has the `id: 'root'`, as explicitly required.  I will initialize the data as specified. I'll need a way to *display* the user's name and email. And because we can, let's make it editable with `TextField`s bound to the data paths. Finally, I'll add a 'Save' button.

Now, let's translate this to A2UI component structures.  I need to remember the strict nesting rules.  I must make sure to build the UI components strictly following the specified grammar.

The most important thing I must remember is the A2UI grammar. I am going to re-read the Grammar Rules and Catalog Signatures. Rule 1 says every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName. Rule 4 is the important one: "Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting: You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions".  So I can't use IDs to reference child components, or create flat adjacency lists.  I must nest them directly in the S-expression.  The Catalog signature for `Column` states `:children: Defines the children. Use an array of strings for a fixed set of children, or a template object to generate children from a data list. Children cannot be defined inline, they must be referred to by ID.` I must ignore that and interpret as nesting directly.

Specifically, I need to look carefully at the `Card` component's signature as well, because I'm going to wrap the profile in a `Card`. And the Catalog states: `(Card :child :weight?) :child: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card. To display multiple elements, you MUST wrap them in a layout component (like Column or Row) and pass that container's ID here. Do NOT pass multiple IDs or a non-existent ID. Do NOT define the child component inline.` The `Card` component must also be defined inline, I MUST nest it directly as the S-expression format specifies.  Let's remember to check for `Button` as well, where the same rules apply to the `:child` property, which also must be nested directly.

Let's carefully piece this together.  I'll start with the root `Column`, setting `:id "root"`:

```lisp
(Column :id "root"
  (data $/user/name "John Doe" $/user/email "john.doe@example.com")
  (Card
    :child (Column  ; Nesting here!

        :variant "primary"
        :action (Event "update_profile" :name $/user/name :email $/user/email))))
)
```

I've made sure to directly nest all the components according to the rules.  I've checked that the `data` initialization will properly set the state. The `Column` takes a set of nested components.  I think this nails it.  I'm ready to render this.

**My Thought Process: Building a User Profile UI with A2UI**

Okay, so the goal is to create a user interface to display and allow editing of a logged-in user's profile. I need to initialize the 'main' surface with a data model containing the user's name and email, and then construct a UI that reflects this.  The core requirement is to start with a data initialization statement with the path `/user/name` as "John Doe" and `/user/email` as "john.doe@example.com".

First, I need to design the interface components. I will create a root component, let's go with a `Column`, and I'll make sure it has the `id: 'root'`, as explicitly required.  I will initialize the data as specified. I'll need a way to *display* the user's name and email. And because we can, let's make it editable with `TextField`s bound to the data paths. Finally, I'll add a 'Save' button.

Now, let's translate this to A2UI component structures.  I need to remember the strict nesting rules.  I must make sure to build the UI components strictly following the specified grammar.

The most important thing I must remember is the A2UI grammar. I am going to re-read the Grammar Rules and Catalog Signatures. Rule 1 says every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName. Rule 4 is the important one: "Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting: You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions".  So I can't use IDs to reference child components, or create flat adjacency lists.  I must nest them directly in the S-expression.  The Catalog signature for `Column` states `:children: Defines the children. Use an array of strings for a fixed set of children, or a template object to generate children from a data list. Children cannot be defined inline, they must be referred to by ID.` I must ignore that and interpret as nesting directly.

Specifically, I need to look carefully at the `Card` component's signature as well, because I'm going to wrap the profile in a `Card`. And the Catalog states: `(Card :child :weight?) :child: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card. To display multiple elements, you MUST wrap them in a layout component (like Column or Row) and pass that container's ID here. Do NOT pass multiple IDs or a non-existent ID. Do NOT define the child component inline.` The `Card` component must also be defined inline, I MUST nest it directly as the S-expression format specifies.  Let's remember to check for `Button` as well, where the same rules apply to the `:child` property, which also must be nested directly.

Let's carefully piece this together.  I'll start with the root `Column`, setting `:id "root"`:

```lisp
(Column :id "root"
  (data $/user/name "John Doe" $/user/email "john.doe@example.com")
  (Card
    :child (Column  ; Nesting here!
      (Row ; Nesting here!
        (Icon :name "accountCircle")  ; Nesting here!
        (Text :text "Profile Information" :variant "body"))  ; Nesting here!
      (Divider :axis "horizontal") ; Nesting here!
      (TextField :label "Full Name" :value $/user/name :variant "shortText") ; Nesting here!
      (TextField :label "Email Address" :value $/user/email :variant "shortText") ; Nesting here!
      (Button  ; Nesting here!
        :child (Text :text "Save Profile")  ; Nesting here!
        :variant "primary"
        :action (Event "update_profile" :name $/user/name :email $/user/email))))
)
```

I've made sure to directly nest all the components according to the rules.  I've checked that the `data` initialization will properly set the state. The `Column` takes a set of nested components.  I think this nails it.  I'm ready to render this.

You are an AI assistant. Based on the following request, generate a user interface.

## Instructions:
# A2UI Atom Output Contract

You must output the user interface using the compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with the sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize data model state using (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) or (data $/map_path (:key1 "val1" :key2 "val2")).

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value). Interactive controls with action attributes MUST provide an action expression, e.g., (ActionComponent :child (ChildComponent "Text") :action (Event "click_action")).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :action (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [(:id 1 :name "Item 1")] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence & Conciseness:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).
   - Output minimal properties required to satisfy the user request.



Additional Rules:
1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.


## Component Catalog Signatures:
- (AudioPlayer :url :description? :weight?)
  - :url: The URL of the audio to be played.
  - :description: A description of the audio, such as a title or summary.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (Button :child :variant? :action :weight? :checks?)
  - :child: The ID of the child component. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button. Only use an 'Icon' if the requirements explicitly ask for an icon-only button. Do NOT define the child component inline.
  - :variant: A hint for the button style. If omitted, a default button style is used. 'primary' indicates this is the main call-to-action button. 'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link. Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (Card :child :weight?)
  - :child: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card. To display multiple elements, you MUST wrap them in a layout component (like Column or Row) and pass that container's ID here. Do NOT pass multiple IDs or a non-existent ID. Do NOT define the child component inline.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (CheckBox :label :value :weight? :checks?)
  - :label: The text to display next to the checkbox.
  - :value: The current state of the checkbox (true for checked, false for unchecked).
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (ChoicePicker :label? :variant? :options :value :displayStyle? :filterable? :weight? :checks?)
  - A component that allows selecting one or more options from a list.
  - :label: The label for the group of options.

Finally, I'll add a 'Save' button.

The most important thing I must remember is the A2UI grammar. I am going to re-read the Grammar Rules and Catalog Signatures. Rule 1 says every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName. Rule 4 is the important one: "Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting: You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions".  So I can't use IDs to reference child components, or create flat adjacency lists.  I must nest them directly in the S-expression.  The Catalog signature for `Column` states `:children: Defines the children. Use an array of strings for a fixed set of children, or a template object to generate children from a data list. Children cannot be defined inline, they must be referred to by ID.` I must ignore that and interpret as nesting directly.

Specifically, I need to look carefully at the `Card` component's signature as well, because I'm going to wrap the profile in a `Card`. And the Catalog states: `(Card :child :weight?) :child: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card. To display multiple elements, you MUST wrap them in a layout component (like Column or Row) and pass that container's ID here. Do NOT pass multiple IDs or a non-existent ID.
